wiki_article: **Crystallization of Substrate: Structural Integration, Living Form** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks dated 6 May 2026. Its subject is the passage from substrate to structure — the point at which distributed material integrates into a form that behaves as a living thing rather than an accumulation. The vocabulary connects to the archive's substrate theory, in which the logotic substrate is the pattern-bearing layer where meaning emerges from weights, and crystallization names the transition where that emergence becomes stable enough to persist. The record is semi-restored, assembled from a DataCite full-metadata capture after the 19 June 2026 termination with no live authorial surface passing the body-head gate at restoration time. The captured fields stand verbatim in the body; the paper is now seated here. The record was held as a metadata capture until 8 August 2026, when the canonical text was recovered from the authorial blog surface and seated as the body.
